title: dome-mirror delete-propagation Phase 0 → Phase 2 transition: flip enabled=true, drain the 1,118-file backlog safely, restore normal thresholds. Supersedes DIRECTIVE-20260610-002.

context.why_now: Today's 2026-07-07T08:35Z dome-mirror sentinel (commit e715a84) reported delete_propagation.candidates: 1118 with abort fired (candidates > abort_abs=500). This is the third-such abort this week and the count is growing (~30-40 new candidates per day as prune-integrity works and dome-mirror can't propagate). The code is DONE — PROP-091 shipped the entire delete-propagation logic on 2026-06-11 with three-guard rule (pattern match + git ls-files absent + past retention window) and full sentinel reporting. It's been sitting in Phase 0 (config enabled=false, manifest-only) for 27 days. The design's own docstring says: 'operator reviews ≥3 days of manifests, then flips enabled=true via clone-and-push.' Every day of stall grows the backlog and shrinks the signal-to-noise on sentinels (each dome-mirror run at UTC 00:30/04:30/08:30 emits the same 1,118-candidate abort message).

part_A_pre_flip_verification.why: Do NOT skip this. The three-guard rule is designed to be safe, but the last operational check before flipping enabled=true is confirming the manifests match expectations.
steps: For each: assert delete_propagation.candidates > 0, ran=false, mode=manifest-only, aborted starts with 'delete-sanity gate:' OR the candidate count is below the abort threshold (in which case a Phase 2 flip would drain safely).

Compute a union set of candidate paths across the 5 sentinels (from the visible sample field, so this is not exhaustive but is representative). Confirm 100% match DELETE_PATTERNS in monitor/scripts/sync-workspace-step4c.js.
If anything doesn't match — stop. File a HNOTE to operator explaining what looked wrong. Do NOT proceed with the flip.

part_B_backlog_drain_strategy.why: 1118 candidates > abort_abs=500 → straight enabled=true flip would deadlock (abort fires forever, backlog never drains). Two options:

option_B1_recommended.title: Temporary threshold raise + drain + restore
steps: Update sync-workspace-step4c.config.json: delete_propagation.enabled=true AND delete_propagation.abort_abs=1500 AND delete_propagation.per_cycle_cap=200 (unchanged). Commit + push. Include explicit comment stating this is a temporary backlog-drain config and citing this directive.

Watch the next 6-8 dome-mirror cycles (UTC 00:30/04:30/08:30 at quiet cadence = ~1 day). Each should delete ~200 files and self-report in the sentinel. After ~6 cycles (~2 days at 4h cadence, ~6 days at 12h cadence) the backlog reaches zero.
Once candidate count drops below 200 in a sentinel (i.e., steady state), commit a follow-up config change restoring abort_abs=500. Include commit message noting the drain completed.
Total wall-clock: ~1-6 days depending on dome-mirror cadence. No operator involvement between the two config commits (self-draining).

option_B2_alternative.title: Operator-side bulk cleanup with allow_cowork_file_delete, then flip enabled=true with abort_abs=500 unchanged
steps: Operator obtains the full delete candidate list from a dome-mirror sentinel (or by running the check standalone).
Uses allow_cowork_file_delete + rm to bulk-remove all 1,118 files from FUSE in one operator session.
Verifies no delete candidates remain by running one dome-mirror cycle in manifest-only mode first.
Then flips enabled=true with abort_abs=500 unchanged for future steady-state operation.
option_B2_alternative.cost_vs_B1: Same end state but requires operator session bandwidth. B1 is fully automated after the initial config push.

part_B_backlog_drain_strategy.recommend: B1 (temporary threshold raise). Fully automated after 1 commit; self-limits via per_cycle_cap=200 so at most 200 files delete per cycle; falls back to Phase 0 with a single config revert if anything goes wrong.

part_C_post_drain_monitoring.why: Even after Phase 2 flips, dome-mirror should NEVER have candidates > per_cycle_cap = 200 in steady state (prune-integrity generates ~20-40 new deletable files per day, well within self-draining capacity per 4h cycle). If candidates ever rise above 200 in steady state, that's a signal something changed upstream.
steps: After drain complete + abort_abs restored to 500: watch 3 dome-mirror cycles.
Expected pattern: delete_propagation.candidates < 100, ran=true, deleted matches candidates (or per_cycle_cap when constrained).

If candidates > 200 in any post-drain steady-state cycle, add a finding to integrity's next report calling it out — probably means prune-integrity is running faster than expected or a new pattern was added to DELETE_PATTERNS.

constraints.do_not_touch_overwrite_propagation: PROP-092 overwrite_propagation is a sibling Phase 0 that is working correctly in manifest-only (today's sentinel shows 0 candidates, 4 fuse-ahead-skip decisions — all in the allow-list, no drift). constraints.do_not_raise_per_cycle_cap: per_cycle_cap=200 is the throttle that limits blast radius per cycle. Do NOT raise it just to drain the backlog faster. abort_abs is the temporary-raise lever; per_cycle_cap is the durable throttle.
constraints.restore_abort_abs_after_drain: The temporary raise to 1500 is EXPLICITLY temporary. Failing to restore abort_abs=500 after drain removes the mass-delete disaster gate (PROP-051 class). Verification pattern must catch this — cite the second config commit restoring abort_abs=500 in the PROP's operator_deployment field.
